audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 3, 4 and 5 disagree with both the packet chart and the already-audited mirror.
audit.why: Packet chart reads Skill, Gragas, Skill, Gragas, Gragas, Gragas, Gragas; the page reads Skill, Gragas, Gragas, Skill, Skill, Gragas, Gragas. Level 3 is your one genuine window (W slow into the E return root before Body Slam is back at 14s); levels 4-5 and 6 are his, because Drunken Rage blunts the burst and Explosive Cask ends any drain you start.
audit.corrected: win[2]/phases[2].side to Skill, win[3]/phases[3].side to Gragas, win[4]/phases[4].side to Gragas, proposed as one group.

audit.why: Spike ordering holds: his level 2 Body Slam, his level 6 cask, his first bruiser item, and your level-3 W-into-E window. Only the mechanics inside spikes[1] were wrong.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two systematic errors. Gragas's sustain is attributed to a 'Q-pool' four separate times, and wants.foe[2] labels Drunken Rage as his Q. Separately, Explosive Cask is said to interrupt Demonic Ascension.
audit.why: Barrel Roll (Q) is a cask that damages and slows — it leaves no healing pool. His sustain is Happy Hour, the passive that heals him whenever he uses a skill, which is also what makes Grievous Wounds matter. Drunken Rage is W: a one-second drink that empowers his next attack and reduces damage taken. And Demonic Ascension is a transform with no channel — Riot's text says the form lasts as long as he drains champions — so the cask does not interrupt it, it knocks you out of the 650 drain range.
audit.corrected: Sustain re-attributed to Happy Hour, Drunken Rage named as W with its wind-up as the burst tell, and the cask reframed as displacement out of drain range.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers behind 'trade around Body Slam'.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s against your Nevermove at 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 — your root comes back marginally faster than his escape, which is the whole reason the level 3 window exists.
audit.corrected: Body Slam's 14s at rank 1 written into early.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Drunken Rage wind-up is never named as a tell.
audit.why: It is an auto-attack reset preceded by a one-second drink — visible, and the moment to step back rather than to trade.

edits.before: At level 1 this is a pure range-advantage skirmish — you can harass with W and autos while Gragas has to walk up to Q the wave, but neither of you has meaningful kill pressure yet. Once he hits level 2 and gets Body Slam he becomes dangerous: a dash into melee puts him inside your W minimum range where the delayed eye hits late and he already has his Q pool running. Play just far enough back that Body Slam does not connect cleanly, and do not step into his Q-pool zone. Your E is available at level 2 as well, but do not throw Nevermove into his Body Slam window — he can E through it and the root whiffs.
edits.after: At level 1 this is a pure range skirmish — you harass with W and autos while Gragas walks up to roll casks, and neither of you has kill pressure yet. Once he hits level 2 and gets Body Slam he becomes dangerous: a dash into melee puts him inside the delay on your eye, and Happy Hour patches whatever chip you traded for. Play far enough back that Body Slam does not connect cleanly, and never stand where a cask is already rolling. Your E is up at 2 as well, but do not throw Nevermove while Body Slam is off cooldown — it is 14 seconds at rank 1, and while it is available he simply rides out of the return wave and the root whiffs.

edits.before: Gragas owns this phase. His W damage reduction eats your Q burst, his E-Q combo wins short trades, and your Demonic Ascension drain is not yet strong enough to overcome his brawl profile in a fight he controls. The correct play is zoning with W threat rather than all-inning him: place Vision of Empire on his Q-pool animation to punish the sustain attempt, then fish Nevermove only when he wastes Body Slam on the wave. Every Soul Fragment you collect through chip damage is real value even if you are not winning the trades. Do not activate R into a Gragas who has his ultimate ready — he will R you out of the drain immediately and you wasted the cooldown.
edits.after: Gragas owns this phase. Drunken Rage eats your Q burst, his E-into-cask wins short trades, and your drain is not yet strong enough to beat his brawl in a fight he starts. Zone with W threat instead of all-inning: his drink has a one-second wind-up before the empowered attack, so treat that as your cue to step back and drop Vision of Empire where he must stand, then fish Nevermove only once Body Slam is spent on the wave. Every Soul Fragment banked off chip is real max health even in trades you lose. And never press R into a Gragas holding his ultimate — he does not interrupt the form, he casks you out of the 650 range and the 120 seconds are gone.

notes: Gragas's sustain was credited to a 'Q-pool' in four places; Barrel Roll has no pool — Happy Hour (passive) is the heal, which is also why the anti-heal line in itemization is correct. wants.foe[2] had Drunken Rage labelled as his Q; it is W, and its one-second drink is an auto-reset tell worth playing around. Explosive Cask was described as interrupting Demonic Ascension in three places: the form has no channel, so the real mechanic is displacement out of the 650 drain radius — same instruction, honest reason. Chart rows 3, 4 and 5 flipped as one matched group to agree with the packet and the mirror. Note the two packets disagree on the win rate for this lane (this side reports 57.89% for Swain over 152 games, the mirror cites 57.42% for Gragas over 256); I followed the mirror and packet for the chart and left diff/diffRating untouched rather than re-rating on contradictory numbers.
